title: Barbara:
title_short: Barbara (Haven resident) · Everybody Has a Story
headline: A Haven resident has to choose between food and medication, and wants people to know that everybody has a story, and that there is help out there.
story: Barbara has to have food, but she also has to have medication. Medication is more important, so she does without food.
People who have never been homeless don't understand: everybody has a story. They are not all drug addicts; many lost their homes to medical issues. Being homeless ages you; she turned gray.
Turn: she has been blessed with this place helping her. Button: take it day by day. Don't give up, because there is help out there.
do: Open on the food-or-medication choice, with the question on screen at 0:00.
Let her say <q>everybody has a story</q> clean, on her face.
Use the side angle (C4902) to hide the joins.
Turn to hope on <q>I've been blessed with this place helping me</q>.
End on <q>there is help out there.</q>
dont: No logo before the end card.
Nothing that pities her. Dignity first.
No other resident's face clear in any B-roll.

decisions.b: The brief's bites go from <q>I turned gray being homeless</q> straight to the button. This plan adds her line <q>which I've been blessed with this place helping me</q> (02:45) before the button so the story lands hopeful (all-clients rule). Nick can drop the THIS PLACE HELPING ME row: the cut is then about 45 s.

client_note: Why this matters: CASS wants real residents telling their own story with dignity, landing on the next step. Barbara's food-or-medication choice is the kind of truth donors remember.
ask_examples: Why is the question on screen at 0:00?
Can I show other residents in the B-roll?
Can I write her last name?
